This new invention, which the inventor calls an "anti-clock," goes beyond tracking time and allows people to control time itself. Despite the revolutionary concept, the inventor admits that the anti-clock is completely useless and does nothing.

By explaining that time is a concept that only exists in the human mind, the inventor ponders the idea that our perception of time is highly subjective and can be manipulated.

Interestingly, despite the fact that the backward clock went against the traditional method of tracking time, the mayor did not consider it revolutionary enough. This demonstrates that the mayor, much like society, still had a traditional mindset regarding the concept of time.

The second invention, the "anti-clock," delves even deeper into the nature of time, challenging the traditional use of timepieces as a mere tool for tracking time. By creating an invention that allows people to control time itself, the inventor successfully pushes the boundaries of human perception. The anti-clock's revolutionary concept aims to shift the focus from tracking time to manipulating and controlling it.
